sources.entry: Kapacitor | Open-source framework for processing, monitoring, and alerting on time series data

summary.one_liner: Kapacitor is an open-source framework from InfluxData for processing, monitoring, and alerting on time series data using the TICKscript DSL.
summary.what_it_does: Kapacitor ships as two binaries: kapacitor, a CLI for calling its API, and kapacitord, the server daemon. Tasks are defined in TICKscript, a DSL, and can be stream-based (as in the example) and operate on time series data. The example script reads cpu_usage_idle measurements, groups by host, applies a 1-minute window with a mean, computes used CPU as 100 minus the mean, and sends alerts when thresholds are crossed. The alert node can route notifications to Slack, VictorOps, or PagerDuty. The README says the command "kapacitord config" will generate an example configuration file, and it links to getting-started and Telegraf TICKscript guides. The README is brief and covers installation, configuration, and a basic example only.
use_cases: alert on high cpu usage from time series metrics
process and aggregate streaming time series data
route monitoring alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or VictorOps
define TICKscript tasks for Telegraf metrics
windowed mean or threshold monitoring of metrics
stack: InfluxDB (implied by dbrp and telegraf references)
notable: TICKscript DSL for defining stream and batch processing tasks
Built-in alert nodes with Slack, VictorOps, and PagerDuty integrations shown in the example
Generates an example config with kapacitord config
Two binaries: CLI client and server daemon
caveats: README gives limited detail on setup beyond install commands and a single example
Depends on time series data being available, with the example assuming a telegraf database
keywords: get notified when cpu is high
